title: If you think you’d like it more than I did, or if you’re REALLY despe...
transcript: Academy Award winner Ethan Coen of the Coen Brothers is the writer of a new anthology play and unfortunately, Aubrey Plaza playing the saxophone was probably my favorite thing about it Ethan Coen actually has a long history with these anthology plays especially at the Atlantic and I've never seen any of them before but this one at least was really not for me as a quick disclaimer I guess it's worth mentioning that I don't even really like the Coen brothers films BUT in a very different way the movies, for the most part, I look at and I'm like okay, I respect what they're doing here it's just not on my wavelength this play though I had more of a visceral negative reaction to it consists of three short plays on the common theme of love and sex at different stages of life it starts with a pair of older people then moving to a group of middle aged-ish people then ending with a pair of young people going on a date and look, I'd be lying if I said I didn't laugh out loud a few times here and there but for the most part the comedy really didn't work for me on one hand, you could just write it off as saying that it's not my sense of humor which fair enough, it's not! there were people in the audience who clearly found it very funny but for me I think it goes a little deeper than that it felt a little at odds with itself to me in the sense that the dialogue is written in this way as if it's trying really hard to sound like intelligent, highbrow comedic Writing with a capital W but meanwhile the content of the humor I actually found to be pretty lowbrow and low hanging and not only did I find it a little too vulgar for my taste specifically I thought it was vulgar in a way that felt cheap and unearned and I'm not usually one to criticize like a distinct stylistic voice like I know some people will say “oh, all the characters talk the same and they all talk like the writer” that doesn't usually bother me but in this case I don't think it was well crafted enough to justify how imposingly conspicuous it was so the whole thing just had this effortful quality that rang very forced to me and frankly I'll say it I think there was more than a hint of misogyny in this play especially the middle act like I never thought seeing Aubrey Plaza and Mary Wiseman on stage together could be anything less than brilliant but the characters they play in different ways lean into sexist tropes of these two-dimensional, vindictive shrews that live to control these more level headed men but yeah aside from some strong performances I found this whole project to be a pretty difficult to stomach on virtually every level and even as someone who doesn't personally love the Coen brothers I still think he can do better than this
